implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy, approved 2026-09-15 and effective 2026-10-01 (P06), now covers OT access, vendor remote access, and acquired systems. OT access procedures for Lakes, Ridge, and the small systems are due with STD-01 (OT security standard) by 2027-03-31.

Regional HMI and engineering accounts are named, requested by ticket, and approved by the ROC Supervisor. Gaps: Lakes, Ridge, and small systems use shared operator logins; OT local accounts are not on the HR termination checklist; access reviews are annual (last February 2026). P07 found 4 of 25 sampled leavers still had active OT local accounts.
evidence: Regional HMI user list; termination checklist; P07 AC-2 sample

implementation_statement: Workforce accounts are created and disabled automatically from the HR feed through the identity provider, which also controls the OT remote access gateway. OT local accounts at Lakes, Ridge, and small systems are outside this automation until they are federated (2027-06-30).
evidence: IdP provisioning logs; gateway group mapping

implementation_statement: The identity provider disables accounts after 45 days of inactivity, which covers gateway users. Local HMI and engineering accounts are not covered.

HMI software at all three platforms enforces view, operate, and engineer levels. At Regional the levels are tied to named accounts. At Lakes and Ridge, shared logins mean the operate level cannot be tied to a person.

At Regional, the IT/OT firewall and OT DMZ enforce deny-by-default flows: historian data moves outward to the DMZ replica only, and remote sessions terminate on the gateway. Gap: the March 2026 site-to-site VPNs from Lakes and Ridge to the ROC allow any-to-any traffic (P07 SC-7 finding).
evidence: Firewall rule export 2026-08-12; OT DMZ diagram

implementation_statement: At Regional, PLC logic changes are made by SCADA engineers and approved by the Plant Manager; operators cannot download logic. At Lakes and Ridge, Integrator B both writes and loads logic with no company approval step.
evidence: Change tickets (Regional); Integrator B work orders

implementation_statement: Regional operators hold operate rights only; engineering rights are limited to 6 SCADA engineers. Gaps: shared engineer-level logins at Lakes and Ridge; Integrator B holds standing administrator access at Ridge.
evidence: HMI role export; P07 AC-6 review

implementation_statement: Administrators use separate admin accounts for the IT/OT firewall, gateway, and cloud. Gap: SCADA servers at Lakes and Ridge are administered with the same shared account used for daily operation.

Privileged access management covers cloud administrators and the OT remote access gateway (just-in-time elevation, recorded sessions). Directory, firewall, and SaaS administrators keep standing rights; extension planned by 2027-03-31.

The gateway and VPNs lock accounts after 10 failed attempts. Control room HMIs do not lock, as the SP 800-82 Rev. 3 OT overlay allows for stations that must stay available for alarm response; the badge-controlled room compensates.
The gateway, VPNs, and engineering workstations display a system use notification stating authorized use and monitoring. HMIs display it at login where the platform supports it (Regional).
Engineering workstations and gateway sessions lock after 15 minutes. Operator HMIs in staffed control rooms stay unlocked by design (OT overlay tailoring), compensated by badge access and cameras.

Regional remote access goes only through the OT remote access gateway: MFA through the identity provider, per-session approval by the ROC Supervisor, session recording, and sessions limited to named targets. Gaps: Integrator B's always-on remote desktop agent on the Ridge engineering workstation (password only, unlogged) and the Lakes on-call VPN (password only). Both move to the gateway by 2026-10-31.
evidence: Gateway configuration and session log; P07 AC-17 test; agent found on Ridge workstation

implementation_statement: Gateway sessions are recorded and logged to the SIEM. The Ridge agent and Lakes VPN are not monitored.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: The gateway and site-to-site VPNs use TLS 1.2 or higher or IPsec with approved algorithms.
At Regional all remote access is routed through the gateway as the single managed access point. Two unmanaged paths remain at Lakes and Ridge (see AC-17).
No wireless access points on OT networks; plant Wi-Fi is business-only and separated by the IT/OT firewall. Quarterly wireless scans at the 4 major plants.
Company mobile devices are managed and cannot connect to OT networks. Gap: Integrator B technicians connect their own laptops to the Ridge and Lakes OT networks.
POL-05 prohibits personal devices on OT networks. Contractor laptop rules are not yet in Integrator B contracts.
Awareness and training policy is part of POL-05 and POL-01 (P06); OT role-based training requirements added in 2026.

All workforce users with email complete annual awareness training and quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 6.4%). Gap: about 110 field and plant staff without company email receive awareness only at hire.
Regional operators and ROC staff completed OT-specific security training (recognizing HMI anomalies, reporting, manual mode) in 2025. Lakes, Ridge, and small-system operators have not.
POL-03 and the logging and monitoring standard STD-02 (draft, due 2027-01-31) set OT logging requirements.
Regional logs gateway sessions, IT/OT firewall, HMI security events, and OT sensor alerts. Lakes, Ridge, and small-system devices log nothing centrally.
Regional HMI events record user, time, tag, and old and new values. Lakes and Ridge records show "operator" only (shared logins).

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews IT and Regional OT alerts 24x7. Gap: no OT playbooks and no escalation path from the MSSP to the ROC; P07 found an OT sensor alert that took 9 hours to reach the ROC.
evidence: MSSP escalation records; P07 AU-6 test

implementation_statement: Regional SCADA, historian, and OT devices synchronize time from a DMZ time source. Lakes and Ridge servers synchronize to the company time source over the VPNs.
Logs forwarded to the SIEM are write-protected; administrators cannot delete them.
SIEM keeps 1 year online. Local Lakes and Ridge HMI event logs roll over in about 30 days.
Audit generation is enabled on Regional components; Lakes and Ridge platforms support limited logging that is not enabled.
The co-sourced internal audit firm assessed 34 IWOS controls from 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21 (P07). Annual assessment cycle.

Written interconnection terms exist for the cloud replica and the 3 client read-only links. No interconnection agreement covers the Lakes and Ridge site-to-site VPNs, the cellular carrier network, or Integrator B access.
POA&M maintained in P07 and reported quarterly to the audit committee.
Operation of the IWOS accepted with conditions on 2026-09-15 (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring covers Regional OT through passive sensors and gateway logs. No monitoring at Lakes, Ridge, or small systems.
Internal connections at Regional (historian, gateway, patch server) are documented in the OT DMZ design. Lakes and Ridge internal connections are undocumented.
Configuration management is covered by POL-01 and the configuration standard STD-03; the OT security standard STD-01 adds OT baselines (draft, due 2027-03-31).
Regional baselines (PLC logic versions, HMI projects, server builds) were recorded at commissioning in 2021 and updated in 2025. Lakes and Ridge have no company baseline.
Regional PLC and HMI changes go through a change ticket with Plant Manager approval and a post-change logic comparison. Lakes and Ridge changes by Integrator B are not ticketed.
Regional changes are tested on the engineering workstation simulator before download. No impact analysis at Lakes and Ridge.
Regional PLC key switches are kept in RUN except during approved changes. P07 found 2 of 4 Lakes PLCs in remote-program mode.
Regional servers are hardened to the vendor's security guide. Lakes and Ridge servers and small-system modems use vendor defaults; 3 modems had web administration reachable from the internet (P07).
Unneeded services are disabled on Regional servers and HMIs; USB ports are locked on Regional HMIs. Not done at Lakes and Ridge.

The Regional OT inventory (passive discovery plus engineering records) is complete. Lakes, Ridge, and small systems rely on integrator drawings; cellular modems are not inventoried. P07 found 11 devices at Lakes not on any list.
Regional inventory is updated with each change ticket. No update process elsewhere.
Operators cannot install software on HMIs; only SCADA engineers can, through change tickets (Regional). Lakes and Ridge HMIs run with local administrator rights (tracked under AC-6).
Contingency planning is part of POL-03 and the contingency and recovery standard STD-06 (draft, due 2026-12-31), and is linked to each system's ERP.

The Regional ERP cyber annex (2025) covers loss of SCADA and manual operation. The Lakes ERP points to the Regional annex, which does not match the Lakes platform. The Ridge ERP review (due 2026-12-24) has no cyber procedures yet.
The Regional ERP was coordinated with the county emergency management office and LEPC in 2025. Lakes and Ridge ERP coordination with their LEPCs is not documented.
Manual-mode drills: Regional twice a year, Lakes once a year, Ridge none since acquisition.
Regional SCADA server rebuild from backup was tested in 2025 (11 hours). No tests at Lakes or Ridge, and no ERP exercise has used an OT cyber scenario.
OT server images and the historian replica are copied to the cloud backup account (separate account, write-once 35 days).
No alternate control room. The standby SCADA server at WTP-R2 will host an alternate ROC position, to be equipped and tested by 2027-06-30.
Regional radio and fiber are independent of carriers. Lakes, Ridge, and small systems depend on one cellular carrier with no alternate path.
Regional PLC logic, HMI projects, and server images are backed up quarterly and after changes to encrypted offline media in two locations. No in-house backups at Lakes, Ridge, or small systems.
Regional backups are verified by comparing restored logic with running logic each quarter. Not applicable elsewhere until backups exist.
Regional recovery procedure documented and tested in 2025. Lakes and Ridge recovery depends on Integrator B with no documented procedure or response commitment.
Identification and authentication requirements are in POL-02 and the authenticator standard STD-04.
Gateway users and Regional HMI users are uniquely identified. Shared logins at Lakes, Ridge, and small systems (named accounts due 2026-12-31 at Lakes and Ridge, 2027-03-31 at small systems).
MFA for privileged access to the gateway, firewalls, and cloud. Not for Ridge and Lakes SCADA server administration (local accounts).
MFA for all remote non-privileged access through the gateway. Gap: Lakes on-call VPN password only.
Regional OT switches use port security for known devices. Not at Lakes or Ridge.

Regional device and service credentials are vaulted and were changed from commissioning values in 2025. Small-system controllers and modems still had default credentials in P07 testing; Lakes and Ridge PLC passwords have not changed since commissioning.
Integrator A and other vendor users have named accounts in the identity provider as guests and use the gateway.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy (P06) covers OT incidents and the public health first rule.
IT responders trained annually; ROC operators trained in 2025; no OT incident training at Lakes or Ridge.
First OT cyber tabletop with the ROC, Ridge staff, and Integrator B scheduled for 2026-11-17 (P08).
IT incidents are handled with the MSSP. The OT runbook (P08) was approved 2026-09-15 and is not yet exercised.
Incidents are tracked in the MSSP case system and the company incident log.
The notification matrix (P08) lists the 24-hour Tier 1 notice, Ground Water Rule reporting, FBI and CISA reporting, and client contract notices. CIRCIA is tracked as proposed only.
MSSP incident response retainer; cyber insurer panel counsel and forensics with OT experience confirmed for 2026.
Incident response plan in POL-03 and two P08 runbooks. Not yet integrated into the Lakes and Ridge ERPs.
Maintenance of PLCs, analyzers, and drives is scheduled in the work order system with records.

Nonlocal maintenance at Regional uses the gateway with approval and recording. Integrator B maintains Ridge through its own always-on agent and Lakes through the password-only VPN; neither is approved per session or recorded.
evidence: Gateway session log; P07 MA-4 test

implementation_statement: Retired OT drives are wiped or destroyed with certificates under STD-05.
USB ports are locked on Regional HMIs; a scanning kiosk checks removable media before use. Lakes and Ridge HMIs accept USB media.
Badge authorization lists for plants and the ROC are reviewed quarterly.
Card access and cameras at all plants and the ROC. Small-system sites have locks and fences only; P07 found one small-system control panel unlocked.
Cameras at all plants are monitored by the ROC; intrusion alarms at wells and tanks report through RTUs (Regional and Lakes). Ridge well intrusion alarms are not wired to RTUs.
UPS units on SCADA servers and HMIs; standby generators at all plants.
Planning policy in POL-01.
This SSP, approved 2026-09-15.
Rules of behavior in POL-05, acknowledged annually; vendor rules of behavior for gateway users.
The Regional OT architecture (zones and conduits) follows SP 800-82 Rev. 3 section 5. No target architecture for Lakes and Ridge yet (due 2027-03-31).
Information security program plan in POL-01 (tailored in: not in the SP 800-53B baselines, needed for program governance).
The vCISO leads the program and the IT Director is the designated security officer, in writing.
Risk management strategy and appetite statements approved 2026-09-15 (P01).
Background checks for all employees at hire, including ROC and SCADA staff.
Identity provider accounts are disabled at termination. OT local accounts and Integrator B accounts are not on the checklist (see AC-2).
Transfers update identity provider groups; prior OT local access is not removed.
Integrator A contract (2025) requires background checks, security training, and incident notice within 24 hours. Integrator B contracts have no security terms.
IWOS categorized High (SSP section 6); OT data classified Restricted under POL-04.
The enterprise risk register (P01) covers the IWOS and is the cyber addendum to the 3 RRAs. The Lakes and Ridge RRAs need the addendum incorporated.

Regional OT vulnerabilities are identified passively from the sensor inventory and vendor advisories monthly. No vulnerability identification for Lakes, Ridge, or small systems; external exposure scans started in P07.
Critical components (chemical feed PLCs, high-service pumps, ROC servers) identified in the BIA (P05). Not yet used to prioritize Lakes and Ridge hardening.
OT purchase requirements (security features, vendor disclosure, support life) are used for Regional projects since 2025. Not applied to acquisitions.
External services in the boundary (Integrator A and B, cellular carrier) are reviewed at onboarding only; no ongoing review.

The Ridge SCADA server and engineering workstation run an unsupported operating system. Compensating controls today: none beyond the VPN. Replacement in the 2027 capital plan; interim isolation behind a dedicated firewall by 2026-12-31.

Regional boundary: IT/OT firewall, OT DMZ, deny-by-default rules (2025). Gaps: any-to-any site-to-site VPN rules from Lakes and Ridge; Lakes historian dual-homed to the Lakes business LAN; 3 small-system modems reachable from the internet.

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny-by-default enforced on the Regional IT/OT firewall. Not on the Lakes and Ridge VPN tunnels.

Historian replication to the cloud and all remote sessions are encrypted. Licensed radio telemetry inside the Regional system is not encrypted (accepted; compensated by protocol filtering at the master radio).

Engineered safeguards that SCADA cannot override: hardwired chemical feed pump stroke limits, hardwired high/low chlorine and pH alarms, and pump fail-safe states at every plant. Verified at all 4 major plants in P07.
Historian replica and OT backups in the cloud are encrypted at rest with company-managed keys; offline backup media are encrypted.
Regional OT patches are applied quarterly after vendor qualification through the DMZ patch server. Lakes and Ridge have not been patched since acquisition.
Vendor-qualified endpoint protection on Regional SCADA servers and HMIs; application allowlisting on Regional engineering workstations. None at Lakes and Ridge.
Passive OT network monitoring at WTP-R1 and WTP-R2 sends alerts to the MSSP. No monitoring at Lakes, Ridge, or small systems; no OT playbooks at the MSSP.
evidence: Sensor coverage map; P07 SI-4 test

implementation_statement: CISA advisories, water-sector ISAC alerts, and vendor advisories are reviewed weekly by the OT security analyst and logged.
Regional PLC logic is compared with the offline known-good copy quarterly and after changes. No integrity checks at Lakes, Ridge, or small systems.
Supply chain requirements for OT purchases since 2025 (Regional). Not applied to inherited Integrator B arrangements.
OT vendors are assessed at onboarding only. No periodic assessment of the 14 OT vendors with remote access; Integrator B never assessed.
